name: Hydrogen
description: Hydrogen's main state at any resonable temperature is gaseous. It only becomes a liquid at -240.21°C. If you lick it at that temperature, not only will you be the first person to lick Hydrogen, you will also freeze your tounge off. However, everything else would be A-OK.

name: Helium
description: Helium is a gas. You can't lick it at any temperature above -270°C, where it then becomes a solid. But at that point you freeze your tounge off. Congrats. Your voice would be a little squeaky though.

name: Lithium
description: Lithium is that acid stuff in coin batteries. Licking it would cause a burn on your tounge, wouldn't taste good, and is bad for your insides if it makes it all the way down.

name: Beryllium
description: Beryllium isn't your friend. Inhaling it (which you probably would do if you were to lick it) can lead to many bad things, even Lung Cancer. It also would burn your tounge. Other than that you are good to go!

name: Boron
lick: Yeah, just don't lick too much.
description: Boron is one of those things that one lick won't hurt, but a lot of licks can cause kidney failure and similar stuff. However, one lick won't really hurt you.

name: Carbon
description: Carbon is 100% safe to lick. (Ever lick the tip of your pencil?)

name: Nitrogen
description: Nitrogen is a gas, so you can't technically lick it unless it is really, really cold (at which point you would freeze your tounge off) but other than the missing tounge you would be fine.

name: Oxygen
description: Oxygen is super, duper common. Without it we would die. However, it is a gas, so good luck "licking" it.

name: Fluorine
description: Fluorine is highly reactive and will burn you badly. Its also a gas, so you would probably inhale it when trying to lick it, which is really bad.

name: Neon
description: It's a gas, so you would have to figure out how to lick a gas, but once you figure that out, you will learn it is harmless.

name: Sodium
description: When sodium touches water, it can fizz, burst into flames, and explode. Not good. Just look up "Sodium + Water" on YouTube. Now imagine that happening on your TOUNGE...

name: Magnesium
description: Magnesium is perfectly fine to lick. Some people actually take magnesium pills.

name: Aluminium
description: Aluminium is super common. From foil to soda cans. If you have ever had a Pepsi or similar, you probably already have licked it!

name: Silicon
description: Small amounts of it is fine, which is what you would get if you were to lick it.

name: Phosphorus
description: Phosphorus isn't your friend. When exposed to air, it catches fire. It also is poisonus, so if you were to get it into your mouth without it blowing up, you would still die.

name: Sulfur
description: It isn't bad for you, it isn't good for you either. So yes, you can lick it and not be harmed, but WHY?

name: Chlorine
description: If you have ever been in a swimming pool, you have probably taken in some chlorine, however, raw chlorine would probably hurt your tounge.

name: Argon
description: Argon is a gas, so you can't get a solid state of it easily, but if somehow you could lick a gas, it would be fine.

name: Potassium
description: Potassium reacts very viloently when it comes into contact with water. Since your mouth has water in it, potassium would react viloently with your MOUTH. That wouldn't be good.

name: Calcium
description: Calcium + the Air = bad stuff. Calcium + your tounge = really bad stuff.

name: Scandium
description: Scandium is one of those rare things. You could lick it and come away from it fine, but good luck finding it.

name: Titanium
description: Titanium is a metal, like steel! It wouldn't hurt a fly (probably).

name: Vanadium
description: Vanadium is in various foods, but in REALLY small amounts. So one lick will be fine.

name: Chromium
description: Chromium comes in various forms. For example, Chromium-6 is bad for you, but Chromium-3 is fine in small amounts. So just make sure you know what you are licking.

name: Manganese
description: In small amounts, it is fine (like in really small amounts). But too much can lead to Parkinson's Disease-Like systems. (BADDDD).

name: Iron
description: Iron is fine to lick. Need I say more?

name: Cobalt
description: Cobalt is fine in small amounts, but it you have too much, it can lead to bad stuff.

name: Nickel
description: Nickel is fine to lick a few times.

_COMMENT: Make a small note in UI saying they can't sue (as a joke of course)
name: Copper
description: Copper is totally okay to lick. I dare you to do it.

name: Zinc
description: People often take some zinc supplements, and they are fine (i think) so licking it can't hurt.

name: Gallium
description: Gallium is just another boring metal. Fun fact: it has a really low melting point! Who knew!

name: Germanium
description: Germainium is totally fine to lick. It is like silicon.

name: Arsenic
description: Arsenic is poison. Please don't attempt to lick it. It won't end very well.

name: Selenium
description: One lick won't hurt. However, if you have 900-1000 micrograms per day, you can lose your hair and nails...

name: Bromine
description: Bromine, a liquid at room temperature, can cause irritation to the skin, vomiting, and more. If exposed, The CDC recommends you take off your clothes. Their words, not mine.

name: Krypton
lick: Yes if you can find it!
description: (not to be confused with Kryptonite) Krypton is a super rare gas found in the atmosphere, lightning, and other small things. It is non-toxic and won't hurt you if you somehow lick it.

name: Rubidium
description: Rubidium reacts harshly with water and air, so by the time it got to your tounge it would be on fire, and from there your day would go downhill.

name: Strontium
description: Strontium can be found in a variety of things, including some toothpaste! So there is a chance you have already licked it!

name: Yttrium
description: Yttrium is rare and is found in LEDs and some cancer medicine! A lick should be okay.

name: Zirconium
description: Zirconium is a rare metal that is fine to lick. Nothing else to say.

name: Niobium
description: Niobium is really strong and can take a lot of heat. You can lick it. It is actually used in jewelry.

name: Molybdenum
description: Molybdenum is fine to lick. Need I say more?

name: Technetium
description: Technetium is radioactive. It really isn't smart to lick anything radioactive. (see: the radium girls)

name: Ruthenium
description: This is one of the rarest stable metals in the Earth's Crust, so you would have trouble finding some to lick, but once you found some, you would find that it is fine to lick, and that it costs $1,675 USD per ounce.

name: Rhodium
description: Rhodium is very reflective and used in a variety of things, among which are catalytic converters! It is fine to lick.

name: Palladium
description: Palladium is used in things like crowns and parts of dentures. If you have that, you might have be licking palladium right now...

name: Silver
description: Silver is used in a lot. There is a good chance something in your home is made out of it. You should lick it.

name: Cadmium
lick: I wouldn't lick this if I were you...
description: Cadmium is very toxic. It can lead to bad things. While one lick might not kill you, it won't feel great.

name: Indium
lick: It is okay to lick, but just don't swollow.
description: Indium is okay to lick, but if you swollow, it could damage some pretty important stuff that you definatly don't want to happen to you.

name: Tin
description: Ever hear of a tin can? Tin is totally fine to lick. In fact, you should lick it, if you have some tin.

name: Antimony
description: Antimony, formerly Stibium, is used in various things including childrens clothing. However, raw Antimony is toxic and can cause respitory damage.

name: Tellurium
description: Tellurium is weird. If you lick it, it can lead to your breath, sweat, and urine smelling like garlic. (weird.)

name: Iodine
description: Iodine is very toxic. 2-3 grams of raw iodine is enough to kill you. While one lick won't get you that much. You definatly won't be feeling good.

name: Xenon
description: Xenon is a gas, so licking it is impossible unless it is super cold, but if somehow you licked it, you would be fine.

name: Caesium
description: Caesium is super soft and melts like wax. However... when it comes into contact with water, it explodes. Highly advised not to lick it.

name: Barium
description: Barium poisoning is a real thing. Licking it could cause nerve, heart, or kidney damage. No bueno.

name: Lanthanum
description: Lanthanum is rare, and is kind of boring. Lick it.

name: Cerium
description: Cerium can ignite when scratched. So I guess in theory you could lick it, just make sure it doesn't come into contact with your teeth.

name: Praseodymium
description: Praseodymium reacts quickly with water, but if you lick it really quickly you should be okay.

name: Neodymium
description: Neodymium is fine to lick. It is used in magents and some other stuff.

name: Promethium
description: This is very, very rare, with less than 600 grams in the Earth's crust. It is also radioactive, so licking it wouldn't be good.

name: Samarium
description: This is a pretty typical metal. When combined with other elements, however, it can be used to do interesting things such as radioactive dating. Who knew!

name: Europium
description: Europium is quite soft and tarnishes quickly in air. One lick should be fine, but looking at the picture, it doesn't look like it would taste good.

name: Gadolinium
description: Another boring, standard, metal. To be totally honest I am just a little over halfway through and am thinking if this is worth it...

name: Terbium
lick: The scientists don't know, so it should be fine.
description: The toxicity hasn't been really tested, but it is considered fine. As a fun fact Terbium is used in naval sonar systems.

name: Dysprosium
description: Dysprosium is a boring metal. Licking it should be okay.

name: Holmium
description: Holmium reacts pretty badly with water, which is on your tounge, so you might not want to lick it.

name: Erbium
description: Yet another boring metal from the Lanthanides group. Yippee.

name: Thulium
description: Thulium is pretty boring. However, it is a metal that can be cut with a knife, which is pretty cool I guess!

name: Ytterbium
description: Ytterbium self-ignites in air when in a powder form, and is also stored in airtight containers when not in use. I wouldn't lick this.

name: Lutetium
description: Lutetium is a boring metal. Totally lickable.

name: Hafnium
description: Hafnium is what is known as a "pyrophoric" element which means that fine particles combust when it is exposed to air. Now, if you lick it juuuusst right you should be fine, but just make sure you don't make any particles.

name: Tantalum
description: Tantalum bonds very quickly with human tissue. Your tounge is human tissue. In addition, OSHA actually posted a legal limit of how much you can inhale of this, and it is a small number, so be careful.

name: Tungsten
description: Tungsten is a very strong and pretty common metal. You can even get weddings bands made out of it!

name: Osmium
description: Osmium is similar to platinum and is totally harmless in it's pure form. Also, fun fact, this is the densest naturally occuring metal!

name: Iridium
description: It is totally fine to lick. That is really all that needs to be said.
